service.name: Private party and dinner party live music
service.serviceType: Live music for private parties, dinner parties and milestone celebrations
service.description: Live music for dinner parties, cocktail parties, milestone birthdays and anniversaries at homes and clubs in Denver, Boulder and across Colorado, solo through quartet.

faqs.q: What does a band for a dinner party cost?
faqs.a: It depends on how many musicians and how long, and for a dinner party that's usually one or two people rather than the band most hosts picture. We don't publish prices; what live music costs across this market is on our pricing page. Describe the evening and we'll tell you which size it wants and what that costs. Signet Artists books private-party musicians across Denver and Colorado.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the band need at home?
faqs.a: A solo sets up in about 6 by 4 feet, a duo in 8 by 6 and a trio in 12 by 8, with no stage; those are working footprints, the space musicians and gear actually occupy. One dedicated 20-amp circuit covers a solo, duo or trio, and a quartet takes two. Dedicated is the word that matters: sharing a circuit with the caterer's warmers is the most common setup problem, and one question to the caterer settles it.

faqs.q: How long does setup take, and what does a club ask for?
faqs.a: Setup takes 45 minutes for a solo and up to 90 for a quartet, before guests arrive, and pack-down 30 to 60 minutes at the end. Tell us where to park and which door to use. Clubs and managed buildings usually ask for a certificate of insurance, and one naming the venue comes with the contract, along with a W-9 and one itemized invoice.

At dinner, a level you talk across without raising your voice, about 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table if the club wants the number. Dancing runs around 88 to 95 on the floor. A shared wall, a close neighbor or a club sound policy goes into the plan at booking, and the night is built under it.

faqs.q: Can you play outdoors at a home?
faqs.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it, and with a move-indoors call time agreed before the day, because Colorado evenings drop fast and instruments and electronics stop behaving in the cold and the wet.
